posts.author: Charibo
posts.body:
Hey all! It's Chari, a solo dev using VX Ace to put together a game for me and my friends. I've been slowly upping the programs I'm using as I experiment with making different games (my last project was quite small but educational, resulting in a short puzzle game that can run on GameBoy hardware). I don't have any expectations of making something for profit, at least not by myself as these have been. And that leads me into the main chunk of this post.
Being solo, some aspects can be harder than others. My favorite part of making games is the core mechanics; the worldbuilding and event creation and watching a story rise from nothing. But that's not all it takes to make a good game. And sure, the RTP has a bunch of fun stuff that I've been using to sidestep actually making assets, but I feel like if I did release anything to the public it would just be skipped over due to looking like a bunch of other games out there. Plus there's just things that aren't prepackaged with the program that I would love to have access to. I'm no stranger to drawing with pencil and paper, but it's very different than the 2013 laptop I'm working on. This has led to me considering AI generation for characters, but it feels like that would be an even worse received move. I can't afford to hire an artist, maybe once or twice but I don't really have a budget for this hobby. That is why I come to you all today; What is your stance on this situation? Is there a limit to how much of a crutch that should be, if I were to use it? What generators would be the most ethical to use? And if none of this is a very good idea, what are some cheap but good ways to do digital art?

posts.author: Charibo
posts.body: That was something I considered, and it's a big mental hurdle. One one hand I want it to feature everything I can dream up, but on the other I know it's frowned upon to use. It was easier to do art myself when everything was 16x16, but this step up in resolution is really daunting on a mousepad. Does anyone have recommendations for programs, or perhaps know of some cheap external hardware I could use to translate hand-drawn into digital?

Click to expand...
Don't use any AI generator to make images for your game. There s no "ethical" one to use, you are better off trying to learn how to draw for yourself if you really can't afford an artist. Your best bet is to do what
@SGHarlekin
said.
There's a few reasons for this:
* You will destroy any good will with your userbase. It's a slippery slope and it becomes hard to trust you after you put it in your game, even if you make the game free.
* AI images in themselves are sloppy and come with a lot of tells that instantly clue in people who know where to look, which make the product even more unprofessional than if you just used RTP.
** Even if the art made looks "good", keep in mind that AI cannot keep details consistent from picture to picture. It becomes obvious if parts of your game look wildly inconsistent from each other, especially if you're too poor to afford a good human artist.​
TLDR; don't. You'll save yourself several headaches in the future.

posts.author: MiguelRPG
posts.body:
If your game is free and not intended for commercial use, I don't see a strong reason to worry about where your assets come from. People have the right to skip a game because of AI content, and we should respect that choice, but it shouldn't stop you from building and finishing your project.
In my view, if this is just a personal project for growth and learning, go ahead and make it with the tools you have. You can always refine things later.
Another practical option is to reduce your scope to match your resources. Instead of creating fully custom protagonists, consider using the built-in RPG Maker generator or pre-made assets for now.
The key is to finish something, learn from it, and build from there.

posts.author: The_Eerie_One
posts.body:
I wouldn't use ai - even if you could somehow find an "ethical" one (which you won't - they've all scrapped the internet and used art from artists without their permission - even with their express disapproval and voiced non-consent) most people just don't like ai and will skip it if they see it (partially because of, again, how they were all trained on stolen art).
I have no skill at drawing, or making pixel art, and unless it becomes necessary I don't see myself taking the time (or having the discipline) to learn. But that's not the only way to make your game stand out - especially if you can build up a following before release. Don't resort to ai.

posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
To your question about inexpensive hardware for drawing--I have a small Wacom Intuos external drawing tablet (the old-fashioned kind, without a screen XD) that I got on sale for $40. Whether or not that's inexpensive in your budget, I can't say, but I can definitely say it's worth the price and has served me well. (I used to recommend Autodesk Sketchbook as a really nice free drawing program, but unfortunately it's been phased out.)
But that said, for the pixel artwork, I never use my tablet. All my sprite and tile art is done with my laptop trackpad. I only use my tablet for character art.

posts.author: ZimXero
posts.body: Avoid using AI.  Your game isn't going to elevate from zero to hero by efficiently using AI.  AI alienates  some players forever and marks the game with a bad reputation from the start.  I recommend using a combination of RTP, creative commons, self drawn, free use - lots on forums, some paid packages, and where needed most a couple salvos of commissioned art or video.  If time is a huge issue, don't get bogged down drawing what you can't.  Draw what you can if it can be done in a timely manner.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Charibo said:
Does anyone have recommendations for programs, or perhaps know of some cheap external hardware I could use to translate hand-drawn into digital?
Click to expand...
Your phone. Most modern smart phones have a "scan" function built into the camera (I think iPhone you have to download an app) . If you align the camera just above the paper, it will automatically crop and straighten the image. From there, use something like Gimp to color correct and remove the background.
You also mentioned something about 16x16 being easier.
Well, VX Ace is 32x32, which is just double the size. So you could just make your canvas 32x32 but color in a 2x2 square for 1 "pixel" (or draw at 16x16 and then scale the image up 200%)

posts.author: Tai_MT
posts.body:
I'll give the tried and true advice I give everytime this sort of thing comes up:
1.  Replace all your assets at the end of the project.  Once you have a game, and it is fun, it takes barely any work at all to just replace things.  You'll save money on assets this way.
2.  Save $5 every week you have the project being worked on.  You can make this more or less, but I stand on $5.  If you work on a game for a year, you now have $260 to spend on assets (more than enough to replace a few character sheets or sprites, I'd reckon).
---
I don't really have much of a stance on AI, other than I hate AI voices and AI generated content as it definitely shows how "low effort" it is, just based on what I've seen on YouTube and Facebook...  As well as how easy it is to trick the demographic known as "bored housewives who spend too much time on tiktok".
I could see it being a boon sometime in the future, but for now, it seems like it's just a low effort crutch, and not even worth considering.
Maybe it'll be a useful tool someday.  For now... it's like asking a baby to do all the work for you, and it definitely shows.
